To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of zeolite as catalyst in mechanical chemical recycling of LDPE waste has caused considerable changes on the properties of the LDPP blends and the treatment of polymeric wastes in presence of catalysts presents potential for recycling polymeric materials with contamination by other polymeric materials and can generate recycled material with improved properties.

the recycling of the low density polyethylene post industrial waste with polypropylene in presence of zeolite and Ziegler-Natta catalysts has potential for the production of recycled materials with improved thermal and mechanical properties.

the mechanical recycling of LDPE waste in the presence of catalyst can generate materials with improved properties and that the use of catalysts is a promising strategy for recycling of thermoplastic waste.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a sustainable process for recycling of LDPE waste with PP.
the development of new technologies for recycling of low density polyethylene and polyproylene waste with the aim to improve the properties of the material.

the recycling of low density polyethylene (LDPE) waste in presence of PP, using thermomechanically and thermally processing of the material, in order to evaluate the influence of zeolite and Ziegler-Natta catalyst on the properties of the blends.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of zeolite as modifier of the structure of polyolefinic waste is a promising alternative to obtain recycled material with improved properties.

the use of ZSM 5 zeolite catalysts in the recycling process of the polymeric waste is an interesting alternative to produce recycled polymeric materials with properties that can be used in the manufacture of new products.

the recycling of polymeric waste is an important alternative for decreasing the volume of the post-consumer waste and the thermochemical treatment in presence of zeolite is an alternative for the recovery of the properties of the material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of the zeolites and Ziegler-Natta catalysts in the recycling of LDPE waste has improved the mechanical properties and the thermal resistance, and has reduced the density of the recycled materials.
the recycling of polymeric waste with high contamination is possible by the use of catalysts, which can be used as modifiers of the polymer structure and improve the properties of the final material.
the mechanical recycling of low density polyethylene with polypropylene is a feasible alternative for the treatment of polymeric industrial waste.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of catalysts in the thermochemical treatment of LDPE/PP blend can generate recycled material with improved properties.
the recycling of the LDPE waste in presence of PP using the thermochemical treatment is a promising alternative to decrease the environmental impact of the plastic waste.
it is possible to recycle LDPE waste with PP in presence of zeolite and Ziegler-Natta catalysts and obtain materials with better properties than the LDPE/30 wt% PP blend without catalysts.
